                                         input, R ETOUCH IQ produces high-quality results across various quality enhancement and style transformation scenarios.

Figure 2. Overview of R ETOUCH IQ. Left: We annotate the user instruction and reasoning for training data. Generated data are filtered to
ensure quality. Middle: The supervised fine-tuning stage. Based on the user instruction (e.g., pop more), the policy model needs to reason
the correct parameters (e.g., exposure) and change them accordingly. Right: The reinforcement learning stage. We leverage a generalist
reward model to propose metrics and provide scalar reward guidance for policy model. Details of the reward model is introduced in Sec 4.

Figure 4. Overview of generalist reward model. Left: Given a before-edited image and a user-edited after image After-u (“u” for
“user”), we perturb the editing process to obtain a suboptimal image, After-w (“w” for “weak”). Middle: In the SFT stage,the reward
model first learns to generate metrics and then produces scalar rewards for the two input images. Right: In the RL stage, we introduce
policy-guided reward training (PGRT), where the suboptimal image After-w is provided by the policy model rather than generated
through perturbation. The goal of the RL stage is to assign a higher scalar reward to the user-edited (strong) image After-u.

As shown in the figure, PGRT shifts the reward model’s dis-                                 We introduced R ETOUCH IQ, an instruction-based MLLM
tribution toward actual policy-generated data, achieving the                                agent that performs executable image editing via profes-
highest accuracy on that set. Next, we use these reward                                     sional software interfaces. By translating natural-language
models to train policy models and report their performance                                  instructions into parameterized edits, it enables control-
on the R ETOUCH E VAL benchmark, illustrated by the bar                                     lable, transparent manipulation beyond black-box diffusion
plot. We observe that PGRT yields the best overall per-                                     methods. A generalist reward model assesses editing qual-
formance, indicating that policy-guided reward training ef-                                 ity, providing human-like feedback for reinforcement learn-
fectively produces a reward model that better supports the                                  ing. This enhances instruction consistency and demon-
policy model’s learning process.                                                            strates the potential of reasoning-based policies with mul-
